findings.issue_text: SpanFlusher.terminate() still reads deleted self.process attribute, raising AttributeError on consumer shutdown
Duplicate source of truth for shard assignment: shards passed both to SpansBuffer constructor and as args to process, risking mismatch between loop iteration and shard_tag/metrics routing
Hot-path connection multiplication: fresh SpansBuffer created per process and on every restart, scaling Redis connections with flusher_processes and churning pools on crash-loops
--flusher-processes click option may not reach ProcessSpansStrategyFactory if the generic consumer bootstrap filters kwargs, making the option inert
New test uses produce_to_pipe, exercising only the threading branch and leaving the multiprocessing spawn path (SpansBuffer pickling, per-process Values, new shards arg in main()) with zero coverage

submit() backpressure check raises MessageRejected for any stuck process but the backpressure metric lacks shard attribution, and the weakened any()-style test cannot distinguish all-healthy from one-dead-shard

Inconsistent metric tag keys: spans.buffer.flusher.produce uses tags={"shard": ...} while spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce uses tags={"shards": ...}, so dashboards grouping by shard miss wait_produce
flusher_unhealthy metric tags a single shard int while the timers tag a comma-joined string, making the flusher health metric ungroupable against the timers due to different tag value types
No test or verification checks metric tag consistency for the new per-shard tags

A negative --flusher-processes value (e.g. -1) yields num_processes = -1, producing an empty process_to_shards_map so zero flusher processes are created, causing shards to stop being flushed and data silently never reaching Kafka while offsets keep being committed
flusher_processes=0 becomes one process per shard via the 'or' fallback instead of raising an error
No validation, test, or documented acceptance criterion for invalid flusher_processes values
test_flusher_processes_limit only asserts structural invariants and never produces a span through a multi-process flusher to verify the message arrives

The core acceptance criterion that segments buffered on shards handled by different flusher processes are all flushed and produced has zero verification; a regression in shard-to-buffer construction would pass both existing tests

The rewritten crash/hang detection and restart accounting in _ensure_processes_alive has no test coverage (behaviors like dead process restart, MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS RuntimeError, and hang detection are untested)

Restart path replaces self.process_healthy_since[process_index] with a fresh Value; if the dict replacement races with a poll the health clock silently resets, and there is no test pinning that restart resets the healthy clock without losing backpressure state
submit() calls record_stored_segments() once per process-buffer instead of once, causing N Redis round-trips per submit with N processes where one sufficed
Unrelated Python style tip added to CLAUDE.md is scope drift not traceable to the PR's stated purpose
_create_process_for_shard is dead code with no call site; if called it would double-spawn processes and leak the old process by overwriting self.processes[process_index] without killing it
buffer constructor parameter used only for len(buffer.assigned_shards); factory still passes full SpansBuffer creating two parallel sources of truth for shard assignments that can silently diverge
Metric tag key inconsistency: produce metrics use tags={"shard": ...} but wait_produce uses tags={"shards": ...}, splitting series across tag keys
if not process: continue in _ensure_processes_alive is always false since Process/Thread objects are always truthy, creating a dead branch for a phantom state
Class docstring says 'Creates one process per shard' but implementation creates min(max_processes, shards) processes with round-robin sharing
Per-shard get_memory_info() called for every buffer on every submit, multiplying Redis calls by shard count on a previously single-call hot path
join() breaks out of the process loop when remaining_time <= 0, leaking processes that are never terminated (N-1 orphaned spawn processes holding Redis connections on slow shutdown)
Metric tag key inconsistency: wait_produce uses 'shards' while other metrics use 'shard', and comma-joined composite shard tag values prevent per-shard filtering and bloat cardinality
_create_process_for_shard is dead code, and calling it would duplicate processes rather than restart, causing duplicate Kafka production
Rebalance abandons old flusher processes without stopping them (close() never sets stopped flag), multiplying leaked processes per rebalance and causing duplicate segment production
max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards) makes flusher_processes=0 mean unlimited processes, contradicting CLI help
submit() memory check aggregates get_memory_info() across N buffers, double-counting shared per-service memory info and skewing the backpressure ratio
'if not process: continue' guard in _ensure_processes_alive can never fire since process objects are always truthy
Test's time.sleep(0.1) is monkeypatched to a no-op, so the wait step does nothing and races remain unguarded
Factory default inverts PR intent: flusher_processes defaults to None making max_processes default to one process per shard, a silent behavior change with no feature flag
Rewritten join() breaks shutdown contract: break exits the loop before process.terminate() is called, so remaining processes are never terminated and can be orphaned
record_stored_segments() now called once per shard-buffer per submit, causing N× Redis round-trips on the hot submit path
Metric tag key inconsistency: wait_produce timer uses 'shards' while sibling metrics use 'shard', fragmenting the tag space for dashboards/alerts
Unrelated scope creep in CLAUDE.md: hasattr vs isinstance doc example bundled into span-buffer multiprocess PR
Dead method _create_process_for_shard(shard) defined but never called, leftover from intermediate design
Dead branch 'if not process: continue' guards a state that cannot occur since processes is never set to None
Test uses time.sleep(0.1) real-wall-clock race instead of deterministic drift synchronization, risking flaky CI
Dropped `self.buffer` reference in `submit`
Per-process restart-state semantics are unclear/risky
`join` timeout accounting is incorrect or problematic

time.sleep(0.1) in test_consumer.py:60 is a no-op because the test monkeypatches time.sleep, so synchronization never actually happens and timing-dependent assertions after step.join() are false confidence

test_flusher_processes_limit only verifies construction, not behavior: it never submits a message or asserts a span written to a shard reaches messages via the assigned process, so shard-mapping regressions in SpansBuffer would pass
The rewritten health-check/restart machinery in _ensure_processes_alive (hang detection, MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS, kill/respawn) has zero tests covering restart behavior

In thread mode, process.kill() is skipped for threading.Thread, so a hung thread is never stopped while a replacement spawns, causing double-flushing or leaked threads, with no test for restart-in-thread-mode
Metrics tag key inconsistency: 'shard' in most flusher metrics but 'shards' in wait_produce, causing dashboards to split wait_produce into a separate series, and no tests assert metric tags
Flusher allows --flusher-processes 0 or negative values, producing an inert flusher with zero processes; spans accumulate in Redis and health monitor falsely reports healthy

Default flusher topology silently changes from 1 process to one-per-shard on deploy, causing a rolling-deploy resource cliff and potential Redis connection-pool exhaustion with no feature flag to revert
join() break on deadline expiry skips terminate() for remaining processes, allowing orphaned old processes to double-flush the same shards during rebalance and produce duplicate segments
submit() memory check double-counts the same Redis service's memory across per-shard buffers, distorting the used/available ratio and delaying or preventing MessageRejected memory protection
_create_process_for_shard single-shard variant is dead code that orphans the process it restarts by not killing the existing process first; deletion candidate
Restart path in _ensure_processes_alive drops in-flight segments popped from Redis but not yet produced to Kafka, with no segment-reclaim mechanism

Silent partial shutdown / process leak: when remaining_time <= 0 the loop breaks, so processes after the current index never get terminate() called and are never joined; spawned flusher processes can survive strategy teardown with a timed-out join, continuing to poll Redis and produce to Kafka for shards the consumer no longer owns, causing duplicate/out-of-order production after rebalance

Thread-mode hang restart produces duplicate producers: in produce_to_pipe mode a hung thread's kill is skipped, then _create_process_for_shards spawns a second thread for the same shards while the hung thread may still wake and run, causing both threads to flush the same Redis segments and produce spans to Kafka twice
The new AttributeError catch converts a visible thread-mode failure into silent data duplication (old code would have crashed loudly)

_create_process_for_shard is dead code with no callers and a misleading comment claiming it 'restarts that process' — calling it would re-create the process without killing the old one, and future wiring through it would inherit the duplicate-producer bug

Inconsistent metric tags: spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes use tag 'shard' while spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce uses 'shards' for the identical value, so dashboards/alerts keyed on one tag silently drop the other timer
Per-shard metric tag multiplies metric cardinality by shard count on every flush cycle — a hot-path tag explosion that should be capped or dropped
--flusher-processes 0 silently means 'unlimited': passing 0 falls through the 'or' to one-process-per-shard, the opposite of a cap, spawning up to len(assigned_shards) processes with no log or error

adjudication_records.issue_text: SpanFlusher.terminate() still reads deleted self.process attribute, raising AttributeError on consumer shutdown

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the single `self.process` attribute and replaces it with `self.processes` (a dict). In `SpanFlusher.join()`, shutdown/termination is performed by iterating `for process_index, process in self.processes.items()` and calling `process.terminate()` on each multiprocessing.Process. There is no remaining reference to `self.process` in shutdown logic, and no `SpanFlusher.terminate()` method shown that would read `self.process`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate source of truth for shard assignment: shards passed both to SpansBuffer constructor and as args to process, risking mismatch between loop iteration and shard_tag/metrics routing

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shards`, the `shards` list used to build `shard_buffer = SpansBuffer(shards)` is the same `shards` list then passed as an argument to `SpanFlusher.main` (via `args=(shards, ...)` while `buffer` is bound to `shard_buffer` in `partial`). The diff shows no divergence between these values, and the `shards` arg is only used to compute `shard_tag` for metrics/tags—not for shard routing—so the claimed mismatch/routing risk isn’t verifiable from this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hot-path connection multiplication: fresh SpansBuffer created per process and on every restart, scaling Redis connections with flusher_processes and churning pools on crash-loops

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shards`, the diff now constructs a new `SpansBuffer(shards)` per process (`shard_buffer = SpansBuffer(shards)`) and stores it in `self.buffers`. On restarts (`_ensure_processes_alive` -> `_create_process_for_shards`), it creates yet another new `SpansBuffer` for the same shard group without any visible teardown/close of the previous buffer object. If `SpansBuffer` encapsulates Redis clients/pools (not shown here), this change can multiply connections with `flusher_processes` and potentially churn/leak resources during crash loops. The diff supports the multiplicative creation pattern; the exact “Redis connection” impact depends on `SpansBuffer` internals, so it’s more an architecture/resource concern than a provable correctness defect from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: --flusher-processes click option may not reach ProcessSpansStrategyFactory if the generic consumer bootstrap filters kwargs, making the option inert

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the click option is added with name `flusher_processes` and the factory constructor now accepts `flusher_processes` and uses it (`max_processes=self.flusher_processes`). However, whether a “generic consumer bootstrap” filters/forwards click kwargs to `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory` is not shown anywhere in this diff, so the claim that the option may be inert cannot be verified from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New test uses produce_to_pipe, exercising only the threading branch and leaving the multiprocessing spawn path (SpansBuffer pickling, per-process Values, new shards arg in main()) with zero coverage

adjudication.rationale: The new test `test_flusher_processes_limit` constructs `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory(..., produce_to_pipe=messages.append)`, which in `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shards` selects the `threading.Thread` branch (`if self.produce_to_pipe is None: ... Process else: ... Thread`). This means the new/changed multiprocessing-spawn path (pickling `SpansBuffer`, per-process `mp_context.Value` dicts, passing the new `shards` arg into `SpanFlusher.main`, and `Process.kill()/terminate()` handling) is not exercised by this test (and `test_basic` also uses `produce_to_pipe`). This is a specific, diff-grounded coverage gap for newly added nontrivial logic, not a proven functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: submit() backpressure check raises MessageRejected for any stuck process but the backpressure metric lacks shard attribution, and the weakened any()-style test cannot distinguish all-healthy from one-dead-shard

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.submit()`, the backpressure path now checks all `process_backpressure_since` values and on trigger does `metrics.incr("spans.buffer.flusher.backpressure")` with no shard/process tags (diff around `submit`, backpressure loop), reducing observability compared to other shard-tagged metrics added in `main()`. The test change to `assert any(x.value for x in flusher.process_backpressure_since.values())` is indeed looser and no longer asserts anything about which/how many processes are backpressured, though it still fails if all are healthy.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent metric tag keys: spans.buffer.flusher.produce uses tags={"shard": ...} while spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce uses tags={"shards": ...}, so dashboards grouping by shard miss wait_produce
flusher_unhealthy metric tags a single shard int while the timers tag a comma-joined string, making the flusher health metric ungroupable against the timers due to different tag value types

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.main`, timer metrics tag `shard` with `shard_tag = ",".join(map(str, shards))`, i.e. a comma-joined string representing multiple shards handled by a process (`tags={"shard": shard_tag}`), while `_ensure_processes_alive` emits `spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy` once per shard with `tags={"cause": cause, "shard": shard}` where `shard` is a single int. This makes it hard/impossible to correlate/group the unhealthy counter with the timer series because the tag values represent different domains (single-shard vs multi-shard string). It’s an observability/metrics consistency issue rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test or verification checks metric tag consistency for the new per-shard tags

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new per-shard metric tags in `SpanFlusher.main`, e.g. `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})`, `metrics.timing(..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})`, and `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})`, plus `metrics.incr(..., tags={"cause": cause, "shard": shard})`. The added/updated tests (`test_basic`, `test_flusher_processes_limit`, and the backpressure assertion change) do not assert anything about metric tag presence or consistency (including the apparent key mismatch `shard` vs `shards`). This is a specific, diff-grounded gap in test coverage for the new observability behavior, not a functional correctness defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: A negative --flusher-processes value (e.g. -1) yields num_processes = -1, producing an empty process_to_shards_map so zero flusher processes are created, causing shards to stop being flushed and data silently never reaching Kafka while offsets keep being committed

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new CLI int option `--flusher-processes` with no validation (can be negative). That value is passed to `SpanFlusher(max_processes=...)`. In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` keeps `-1`, then `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(...))` becomes `-1`, making `process_to_shards_map` empty (`range(-1)`), and the subsequent shard assignment loop does `self.process_to_shards_map[process_index].append(...)`, which will raise at runtime (empty dict). So a negative value breaks flusher setup (though it would error rather than silently continue).

adjudication_records.issue_text: flusher_processes=0 becomes one process per shard via the 'or' fallback instead of raising an error

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats `max_processes=0` as falsy and falls back to `len(buffer.assigned_shards)`. That makes `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(...))` equal to the shard count, effectively creating one process per shard instead of respecting the explicit `0` value or rejecting it. This behavior is directly implied by the diff and is likely unintended for a CLI-configured `--flusher-processes` value.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No validation, test, or documented acceptance criterion for invalid flusher_processes values

adjudication.rationale: The new `flusher_processes`/`max_processes` plumbing has no validation and can lead to incorrect or crashing behavior for invalid values. In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` means `0` is treated as falsy and silently becomes `len(...)` (ignoring the user's value). Worse, negative values are truthy, so `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(...))` can become negative; then `process_to_shards_map` is built with `range(self.num_processes)` (empty), but later `process_index = i % self.num_processes` and `self.process_to_shards_map[process_index].append(shard)` will fail because the map has no such key. The click option is `type=int` with no bounds, and tests only cover a valid limit (`flusher_processes=2`), not invalid inputs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: test_flusher_processes_limit only asserts structural invariants and never produces a span through a multi-process flusher to verify the message arrives

adjudication.rationale: In `test_flusher_processes_limit`, the test only checks internal bookkeeping (`len(flusher.processes)`, `max_processes`, `num_processes`, and shard distribution via `process_to_shards_map`) and then calls `step.join()` without ever submitting messages/spans or asserting anything about output in `messages`. Given the diff adds nontrivial shard-to-process mapping and per-process flushing/metrics paths in `SpanFlusher` (e.g., `process_to_shards_map`, `buffers`, `process_backpressure_since`, `SpanFlusher.main(..., shards=...)`), this test does not validate that a multi-worker flusher actually flushes and delivers produced Kafka payloads.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The core acceptance criterion that segments buffered on shards handled by different flusher processes are all flushed and produced has zero verification; a regression in shard-to-buffer construction would pass both existing tests

adjudication.rationale: Diff introduces per-process shard buffers in `SpanFlusher` (`shard_buffer = SpansBuffer(shards)` and `self.buffers[process_index] = shard_buffer`) plus shard-to-process mapping (`process_to_shards_map`). The new test `test_flusher_processes_limit` only asserts process count and shard distribution (lengths), and `test_basic`/`test_flusher` don’t assert that buffered segments from multiple shards handled by different flusher processes are actually flushed/produced. So a regression where shard-to-buffer construction or shard assignment breaks flushing for some shards could still pass these tests; this is a concrete missing verification for newly added nontrivial multiprocessing/sharding logic, not a proven runtime defect in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The rewritten crash/hang detection and restart accounting in _ensure_processes_alive has no test coverage (behaviors like dead process restart, MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS RuntimeError, and hang detection are untested)

adjudication.rationale: The diff substantially rewrites flusher liveness checking from a single-process `_ensure_process_alive` to multi-process `_ensure_processes_alive`, including per-process `process_healthy_since`, `process_restarts`, kill/recreate behavior, and raising `RuntimeError` after `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` (see `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py`). The added/updated tests only cover process-count limiting and shard distribution (`test_flusher_processes_limit`) and backpressure flag presence (`test_flusher.py`), but do not exercise any of the new restart/hang paths (dead process restart, hang detection via `healthy_since`, or the repeated-crash `RuntimeError`). This is a specific missing-coverage issue for newly added nontrivial logic rather than a proven functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Restart path replaces self.process_healthy_since[process_index] with a fresh Value; if the dict replacement races with a poll the health clock silently resets, and there is no test pinning that restart resets the healthy clock without losing backpressure state

adjudication.rationale: In the restart path, `_create_process_for_shards` does **not** replace `self.process_healthy_since[process_index]` with a new `multiprocessing.Value`; it only mutates the existing one via `self.process_healthy_since[process_index].value = int(time.time())` (same for backpressure values). The dict entries are created once in `__init__` and are never reassigned in the shown diff, so the claimed “fresh Value” replacement/race does not exist in this patch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: submit() calls record_stored_segments() once per process-buffer instead of once, causing N Redis round-trips per submit with N processes where one sufficed

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.submit()`, the diff changes `self.buffer.record_stored_segments()` to a loop: `for buffer in self.buffers.values(): buffer.record_stored_segments()` (new multi-process/shard buffers). That does make the method run once per per-process `SpansBuffer`, i.e. O(num_processes) per submit. Whether this causes “N Redis round-trips” specifically isn’t provable from the diff (implementation of `record_stored_segments()` isn’t shown), but the finding correctly flags a concrete potential performance regression introduced by the new per-process buffer design.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unrelated Python style tip added to CLAUDE.md is scope drift not traceable to the PR's stated purpose

adjudication.rationale: The diff includes an added section in `CLAUDE.md` about using `isinstance()` instead of `hasattr()` for unions, which is unrelated to the main code changes around span flusher multiprocessing and new CLI options. This is a reviewable scope/cleanup concern (unrelated documentation/style tip bundled into a functional PR), though the claim about the PR’s “stated purpose” is not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: _create_process_for_shard is dead code with no call site; if called it would double-spawn processes and leak the old process by overwriting self.processes[process_index] without killing it

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int)` is defined but has no call site (only `_create_processes`, `_create_process_for_shards`, and `_ensure_processes_alive` are used). So it is dead code as shown. Also, if it were called, it directly invokes `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` without terminating/killing the existing process/thread for that `process_index`, and `_create_process_for_shards` overwrites `self.processes[process_index]` after starting a new one—so the old worker could be left running (especially in the thread case, where no kill/terminate happens). This is a real diff-grounded maintainability/safety issue, but not an immediately triggered defect since there is no call path in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: buffer constructor parameter used only for len(buffer.assigned_shards); factory still passes full SpansBuffer creating two parallel sources of truth for shard assignments that can silently diverge

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, the passed `buffer: SpansBuffer` is not stored/used after initialization; it’s only consulted to compute `self.max_processes` (via `len(buffer.assigned_shards)`) and to build `process_to_shards_map` by iterating `buffer.assigned_shards`. The flusher then creates new per-process `SpansBuffer(shards)` instances (`shard_buffer`) and stores those in `self.buffers`. This does mean the factory passes a full `SpansBuffer` but the flusher operates on newly constructed buffers, which is an architectural/clarity concern and could allow inconsistency if shard assignment were ever to change elsewhere (not shown in the diff), but it’s not a directly verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Metric tag key inconsistency: produce metrics use tags={"shard": ...} but wait_produce uses tags={"shards": ...}, splitting series across tag keys
matched_golden_ids: In the SpanFlusher flush loop, metric tags inconsistently use 'shard' (e.g., in spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes) and 'shards' (in spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce) for the same shard identifier value. This prevents correct metric aggregation across flush stages — dashboards and alerts filtering by tag 'shard' will miss data tagged as 'shards' and vice versa.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same inconsistency in metric tag keys ('shard' vs 'shards') between produce and wait_produce metrics, leading to split metric series and incorrect aggregation, which matches the golden issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: if not process: continue in _ensure_processes_alive is always false since Process/Thread objects are always truthy, creating a dead branch for a phantom state

adjudication.rationale: In `_ensure_processes_alive`, `for process_index, process in self.processes.items(): if not process: continue` is indeed effectively dead because `self.processes` is populated with `multiprocessing.Process`/`threading.Thread` instances in `_create_process_for_shards`, and those objects are always truthy. However, this is just redundant/defensive code and does not create broken behavior; it’s a minor style/nit rather than a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Class docstring says 'Creates one process per shard' but implementation creates min(max_processes, shards) processes with round-robin sharing

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher` class docstring, it states: "Creates one process per shard for parallel processing." However, the implementation in `__init__` computes `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` and assigns shards round-robin via `process_index = i % self.num_processes`, meaning multiple shards can share a single process when `max_processes` is less than shard count. This is a diff-grounded documentation/behavior mismatch, not a functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Per-shard get_memory_info() called for every buffer on every submit, multiplying Redis calls by shard count on a previously single-call hot path

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.submit`, the diff changes `memory_infos = list(self.buffer.get_memory_info())` to iterating `for buffer in self.buffers.values(): memory_infos.extend(buffer.get_memory_info())`. This does add one `get_memory_info()` call per per-process buffer, but the diff also splits shards across these buffers (`SpansBuffer(shards)` per process). Nothing in the diff shows a per-shard `get_memory_info()` being called for *every* buffer (i.e., shard_count multiplication); rather, shards appear partitioned across buffers, so total shard coverage should remain ~once overall, not N×N. The finding overstates the effect and isn’t verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: join() breaks out of the process loop when remaining_time <= 0, leaking processes that are never terminated (N-1 orphaned spawn processes holding Redis connections on slow shutdown)
Metric tag key inconsistency: wait_produce uses 'shards' while other metrics use 'shard', and comma-joined composite shard tag values prevent per-shard filtering and bloat cardinality

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.main`, metric tags are inconsistent: `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timing("spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes", ..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})` use the key `shard`, but `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})` uses `shards`. Also, `shard_tag` is built as a comma-joined list of shard ids (`shard_tag = ",".join(map(str, shards))`), so the tag value represents a shard-group (e.g. "0,1") rather than a single shard, which impedes per-shard filtering and can increase tag-value cardinality as shard-group combinations vary with `process_to_shards_map`. This is an observability/metrics design issue, not a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: _create_process_for_shard is dead code, and calling it would duplicate processes rather than restart, causing duplicate Kafka production

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `_create_process_for_shard` is introduced but never referenced/called anywhere (new code uses `_create_processes`, `_create_process_for_shards`, and `_ensure_processes_alive`), so it is dead code. Also, `_create_process_for_shard` simply calls `_create_process_for_shards(...)`, and `_create_process_for_shards` starts a new process/thread and overwrites `self.processes[process_index]` without terminating/joining any existing one for that index; so if it were called while an existing worker were still running, it would indeed risk duplicating workers and could lead to duplicate Kafka production. However, that duplication is hypothetical from this diff because the method is unused here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Rebalance abandons old flusher processes without stopping them (close() never sets stopped flag), multiplying leaked processes per rebalance and causing duplicate segment production

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `SpanFlusher.close()` only calls `self.next_step.close()` and does not set `self.stopped.value = True` or terminate/join any of the spawned processes/threads. The stop signal is only set in `join()`. If the strategy lifecycle calls `close()` without a guaranteed subsequent `join()` (e.g., during rebalance/teardown paths), the flusher workers could keep running and be effectively “orphaned.” However, the claim about rebalance definitely causing leaked/duplicated production is not directly verifiable from the diff because the consumer’s close/join invocation order isn’t shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards) makes flusher_processes=0 mean unlimited processes, contradicting CLI help

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats a provided `max_processes=0` as falsy and replaces it with `len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, effectively removing the limit and spawning one process per shard (via `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))`). This makes `--flusher-processes=0` behave like “unlimited/max”, which is inconsistent with the CLI option described as a maximum number of processes and can lead to unexpectedly high process counts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: submit() memory check aggregates get_memory_info() across N buffers, double-counting shared per-service memory info and skewing the backpressure ratio

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change the memory check in `SpanFlusher.submit()` to aggregate `get_memory_info()` across all per-process `SpansBuffer` instances (`memory_infos.extend(buffer.get_memory_info())`). While this could duplicate entries if multiple buffers report the same underlying service, the finding’s specific claim that this “skew[s] the backpressure ratio” is not supported by what’s shown: the ratio is computed as `sum(used) / sum(available)`, so exact duplicate per-service entries would scale numerator and denominator equally and not change the ratio. Whether `get_memory_info()` returns shared-per-service vs per-shard data (and thus whether duplication is real) is not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: 'if not process: continue' guard in _ensure_processes_alive can never fire since process objects are always truthy

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `self.processes` is populated in `_create_process_for_shards` with a started `process` object (`multiprocessing` Process or `threading.Thread`) and typed as `dict[int, SpawnProcess | threading.Thread]` (no `None`). Such objects are normally truthy, so `if not process: continue` is just redundant/dead code, not a functional defect. The finding frames this as an issue, but it’s at most a minor style nit and not a verifiable bug from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test's time.sleep(0.1) is monkeypatched to a no-op, so the wait step does nothing and races remain unguarded
matched_golden_ids: The test_basic function in test_consumer.py uses a monkeypatched time.sleep that returns immediately, but then calls time.sleep(0.1) expecting it to actually wait.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe that in test_basic the time.sleep function has been monkeypatched to return immediately (no-op), yet the test later calls time.sleep(0.1) as if it would actually wait, meaning the intended delay does not occur and timing/race issues may result.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Factory default inverts PR intent: flusher_processes defaults to None making max_processes default to one process per shard, a silent behavior change with no feature flag

adjudication.rationale: In `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory.__init__`, `flusher_processes` is added with default `None`, and passed through as `max_processes=self.flusher_processes` to `SpanFlusher`. In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` means `None` results in `len(assigned_shards)` (i.e., up to one process per shard). While the Click wiring sets a default of `1` for `--flusher-processes`, any non-Click/programmatic construction of the factory that omits `flusher_processes` will now default to per-shard process fanout, which is a potentially surprising behavioral change and worth calling out, but not an intrinsically verifiable correctness defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Rewritten join() breaks shutdown contract: break exits the loop before process.terminate() is called, so remaining processes are never terminated and can be orphaned
record_stored_segments() now called once per shard-buffer per submit, causing N× Redis round-trips on the hot submit path

adjudication.rationale: In SpanFlusher.submit(), the diff changes a single call `self.buffer.record_stored_segments()` to a loop over all per-process shard buffers: `for buffer in self.buffers.values(): buffer.record_stored_segments()` (src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py). Since `self.buffers` is populated with one SpansBuffer per flusher process/shard-group, this increases the number of record_stored_segments() invocations per submit from 1 to `len(self.buffers)` (up to `num_processes`). That’s a concrete hot-path performance regression risk; while the diff doesn’t show the internals of record_stored_segments(), the review concern about multiplying external/Redis work is plausibly grounded in this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Metric tag key inconsistency: wait_produce timer uses 'shards' while sibling metrics use 'shard', fragmenting the tag space for dashboards/alerts

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py`, the diff introduces metric tags keyed as `shard` for `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes`, but uses `shards` for `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` (`metrics.timer(..., tags={"shards": shard_tag})`). This is a real, diff-grounded inconsistency that would split time series across two tag keys, impacting dashboards/alerts, but it does not break runtime correctness.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unrelated scope creep in CLAUDE.md: hasattr vs isinstance doc example bundled into span-buffer multiprocess PR

adjudication.rationale: The diff includes an unrelated documentation change in CLAUDE.md adding a "WRONG/RIGHT" example about using hasattr() vs isinstance() for unions, while the rest of the PR changes span flusher multiprocessing and related CLI/tests. This supports the finding that the PR bundles unrelated scope creep (doc guidance) into a functional span-buffer multiprocess change, which is a review/maintainability concern rather than a runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead method _create_process_for_shard(shard) defined but never called, leftover from intermediate design

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py`, `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int)` is added (after `_create_process_for_shards`) but there are no call sites shown in the diff; the rest of the class uses `_create_process_for_shards` / `_ensure_processes_alive` for restarts. As written, it appears to be unused/dead code, likely leftover from an intermediate design, which is a maintainability issue rather than a runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead branch 'if not process: continue' guards a state that cannot occur since processes is never set to None

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive`, the loop includes `if not process: continue` while `self.processes` is populated only with started `Process`/`Thread` objects in `_create_process_for_shards` (`self.processes[process_index] = process`) and is never assigned `None` anywhere in the diff. Since these objects are truthy, the guard is effectively dead code (cleanup/simplification opportunity) but not a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test uses time.sleep(0.1) real-wall-clock race instead of deterministic drift synchronization, risking flaky CI

adjudication.rationale: In `tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py::test_basic`, the test monkeypatches `time.sleep` to `lambda _: None` (`monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`) before the added `time.sleep(0.1)` call. Because `import time` refers to the same `time` module whose `sleep` was patched, the `time.sleep(0.1)` is not a real wall-clock delay and does not introduce a real-time race as claimed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dropped `self.buffer` reference in `submit`

adjudication.rationale: While `self.buffer = buffer` was removed in `SpanFlusher.__init__`, the diff shows this was replaced with per-process/per-shard buffers stored in `self.buffers`. Accordingly, `submit()` was updated from `self.buffer.record_stored_segments()` to `for buffer in self.buffers.values(): buffer.record_stored_segments()`, and similarly for `get_memory_info()`. There is no remaining `self.buffer` usage in `submit()`, and the new logic appears intentional rather than a dropped/forgotten reference.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Per-process restart-state semantics are unclear/risky

adjudication.rationale: The refactor introduces per-process state (`process_restarts`, `process_healthy_since`, `process_backpressure_since`) keyed by `process_index` in `SpanFlusher.__init__`, and `_ensure_processes_alive()` now decides whether to restart/raise per process. However, the restart-state semantics are not clearly defined and could be risky: `process_restarts[process_index]` is only incremented and never reset on recovery (same pattern as before, but now multiplied across multiple processes), so intermittent failures over a long runtime can eventually trip `> MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` and restart the whole consumer even if failures were long ago. Also the comment in `_create_process_for_shards` says to "Keep back pressure across the restart", and indeed `process_backpressure_since[...]` is preserved, which may retain stale backpressure across a recreated process and affect unrelated shards handled by that process group.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `join` timeout accounting is incorrect or problematic

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.join`, timeout accounting is inconsistent: it computes a `deadline` but then calls `self.next_step.join(timeout)` with the original timeout (not the remaining time), so time spent waiting on `next_step` is not subtracted and total blocking can exceed the requested timeout. Additionally, inside the per-process loop it computes `remaining_time = deadline - time.time()` but never uses it to bound sleeps/joins; it only breaks if <= 0, while the inner `while process.is_alive() ...` loop continues sleeping in 0.1s increments up to (and potentially slightly past) the deadline. This makes the join timeout behavior problematic and not accurately respected across multiple components.

adjudication_records.issue_text: time.sleep(0.1) in test_consumer.py:60 is a no-op because the test monkeypatches time.sleep, so synchronization never actually happens and timing-dependent assertions after step.join() are false confidence
matched_golden_ids: Sleep in test_consumer.py won’t actually wait because time.sleep was monkeypatched above; consider restoring sleep or using a different sync to ensure the flusher has time to process.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments identify the same underlying issue: in test_consumer.py, time.sleep is monkeypatched, so a later time.sleep call does not actually wait, making synchronization/timing assertions unreliable. The candidate also notes this leads to false confidence after join(), aligning with the golden concern about ensuring the flusher has time to process.

adjudication_records.issue_text: test_flusher_processes_limit only verifies construction, not behavior: it never submits a message or asserts a span written to a shard reaches messages via the assigned process, so shard-mapping regressions in SpansBuffer would pass

adjudication.rationale: In `test_flusher_processes_limit`, the assertions only cover configuration/state (`len(flusher.processes)`, `max_processes`, `num_processes`, and that `process_to_shards_map` totals 4 shards). The test never exercises the new per-process/per-shard execution path in `SpanFlusher` (e.g., the per-process `SpansBuffer(shards)` creation in `_create_process_for_shards` and producing via `SpanFlusher.main`), since it does not `submit` any messages or assert anything arrives in `messages`. That means a regression where shard-to-buffer/process wiring is wrong could still pass this test despite the new nontrivial shard mapping logic added in `flusher.py`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The rewritten health-check/restart machinery in _ensure_processes_alive (hang detection, MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS, kill/respawn) has zero tests covering restart behavior

adjudication.rationale: The diff substantially rewrites flusher liveness/restart logic: `_ensure_processes_alive` now iterates `self.processes`, detects dead processes (`not process.is_alive()`), hang via `time.time() - self.process_healthy_since[...]`, increments `self.process_restarts[...]`, may `kill()` and respawn via `_create_process_for_shards`, and enforces `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS`. The added/modified tests cover process count limiting (`test_flusher_processes_limit`) and backpressure values (`test_flusher`), but none simulate a process/thread dying or the hang timeout to assert restart/kill/respawn and MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS behavior. So the finding (no tests for restart behavior) is diff-grounded and actionable, but it’s a test coverage gap rather than a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In thread mode, process.kill() is skipped for threading.Thread, so a hung thread is never stopped while a replacement spawns, causing double-flushing or leaked threads, with no test for restart-in-thread-mode

adjudication.rationale: In thread mode (`produce_to_pipe is not None`), `_create_process_for_shards` uses `threading.Thread` (not a `multiprocessing.Process`). When `_ensure_processes_alive` detects an unhealthy flusher (either `not process.is_alive()` or `hang` via `process_healthy_since[...]`), it only attempts `process.kill()` if `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`, so a hung `threading.Thread` cannot be stopped. The code then unconditionally calls `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`, spawning a replacement thread while the old hung thread may still be running (or stuck), leading to leaked threads and potentially duplicated flushing work. The added tests cover process limiting and backpressure mapping but do not exercise the restart/unhealthy path in thread mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Metrics tag key inconsistency: 'shard' in most flusher metrics but 'shards' in wait_produce, causing dashboards to split wait_produce into a separate series, and no tests assert metric tags

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.main`, most metrics use tag key `shard` (e.g. `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timing(..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})`), but `wait_produce` uses `tags={"shards": shard_tag}`. This diff-grounded inconsistency would split the `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` series from other shard-tagged metrics in dashboards, but it doesn’t break runtime behavior. The added/updated tests (`test_consumer.py`, `test_flusher.py`) assert process counts/backpressure values and do not assert metric tag keys/values.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Flusher allows --flusher-processes 0 or negative values, producing an inert flusher with zero processes; spans accumulate in Redis and health monitor falsely reports healthy

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not support the claim that `--flusher-processes 0` yields an inert flusher with zero processes. In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, so a passed `0` (falsy) falls back to `len(buffer.assigned_shards)` and will still create processes for shards. A negative value is truthy and would instead lead to `self.num_processes = min(negative, len(...))` (negative), which would likely crash during shard assignment (`process_index = i % self.num_processes` then `process_to_shards_map[process_index].append(...)` on an empty map), not silently run with zero processes or report healthy.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Default flusher topology silently changes from 1 process to one-per-shard on deploy, causing a rolling-deploy resource cliff and potential Redis connection-pool exhaustion with no feature flag to revert

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes SpanFlusher from a single background worker to spawning multiple workers based on shard assignment: `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` and `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))`, then `_create_processes()` creates one process/thread per `process_index` (often one-per-shard when `max_processes` is unset). That is a real, diff-grounded operational/architecture concern because it can increase process/thread count and per-process Redis usage. However, it’s not a directly verifiable correctness defect, and the diff also adds a limiting knob (`--flusher-processes` / `flusher_processes`) to cap processes, so the claim that there is “no way to revert” is overstated and the exact deploy default depends on wiring not shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: join() break on deadline expiry skips terminate() for remaining processes, allowing orphaned old processes to double-flush the same shards during rebalance and produce duplicate segments

adjudication.rationale: In SpanFlusher.join(), if a timeout is provided and the computed remaining_time <= 0, the loop `break`s out of iterating over `self.processes` (see the `if remaining_time <= 0: break`). Because the `process.terminate()` call is inside that per-process loop, any processes not yet visited will not be terminated at all. This can leave flusher processes running after join() returns when the deadline is exhausted. The follow-on claim about duplicate flushing during rebalance is plausible but not directly verifiable from the diff; the orphan-process behavior itself is verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: submit() memory check double-counts the same Redis service's memory across per-shard buffers, distorting the used/available ratio and delaying or preventing MessageRejected memory protection

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.submit()`, the diff changes the memory check from `list(self.buffer.get_memory_info())` to aggregating `buffer.get_memory_info()` across `self.buffers` (per-process shard buffers). While this could duplicate the same Redis service’s memory info, the code sums both `used` and `available` across all entries; if the same service is duplicated, both numerator and denominator would scale together and the `used/available` ratio would not be distorted based on what’s shown. The diff does not show what `SpansBuffer.get_memory_info()` returns (per-service vs per-shard, deduped or not), so the claim that it “double-counts” and alters rejection behavior is not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: _create_process_for_shard single-shard variant is dead code that orphans the process it restarts by not killing the existing process first; deletion candidate

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shard`, which is not referenced anywhere else in the shown changes (the liveness path uses `_create_process_for_shards` after killing the existing process). As written, `_create_process_for_shard` calls `_create_process_for_shards` without terminating an existing process for that `process_index`, and would overwrite `self.processes[process_index]`, potentially leaving the prior process running if this method is ever used. However, the diff alone doesn’t prove it’s actually dead code project-wide or that it’s invoked, so this is best treated as a maintainability/latent-risk issue rather than a confirmed behavioral defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Restart path in _ensure_processes_alive drops in-flight segments popped from Redis but not yet produced to Kafka, with no segment-reclaim mechanism

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `_ensure_processes_alive` killing/restarting worker processes/threads (and recreating per-shard `SpansBuffer` instances), but it does not show how segments are fetched from Redis (e.g., whether they are destructively popped/acked) or whether any reclaim/visibility-timeout mechanism exists inside `SpansBuffer`/Redis operations. Without that code, the claim that restarts "drop in-flight segments popped from Redis" is not verifiable from the diff alone; at most it’s a speculative reliability concern based on unseen buffer semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Silent partial shutdown / process leak: when remaining_time <= 0 the loop breaks, so processes after the current index never get terminate() called and are never joined; spawned flusher processes can survive strategy teardown with a timed-out join, continuing to poll Redis and produce to Kafka for shards the consumer no longer owns, causing duplicate/out-of-order production after rebalance
matched_golden_ids: Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate highlights that breaking the loop when remaining_time<=0 prevents terminate()/join from being called on later flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown—same core issue as the golden comment about skipping termination when the deadline is exceeded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Thread-mode hang restart produces duplicate producers: in produce_to_pipe mode a hung thread's kill is skipped, then _create_process_for_shards spawns a second thread for the same shards while the hung thread may still wake and run, causing both threads to flush the same Redis segments and produce spans to Kafka twice

adjudication.rationale: In `produce_to_pipe` mode, `_create_process_for_shards` uses `threading.Thread` (not a `multiprocessing.Process`). In `_ensure_processes_alive`, a “hang” is detected when `time.time() - process_healthy_since[...] > max_unhealthy_seconds` even if the thread is still `is_alive()`. On restart, the code only attempts to kill if `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`, so the hung thread is not stopped, and `_create_process_for_shards` starts a new thread for the same shard set. Since both threads share the same `stopped` flag (still false) and operate on the same Redis shards, the original thread could later resume and flush/produce concurrently, plausibly duplicating produced spans.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The new AttributeError catch converts a visible thread-mode failure into silent data duplication (old code would have crashed loudly)

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive`, when a flusher worker is a `threading.Thread` (used when `produce_to_pipe` is not `None`), an unhealthy-but-still-alive thread (the `cause == "hang"` branch) will be “restarted” via `_create_process_for_shards(...)` without any attempt to stop/kill the existing thread because the code only calls `process.kill()` when `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. This can leave the old thread running while starting a new one for the same shard set, which can lead to concurrent flushing/producing for the same shards (potential duplication). Previously, the code unconditionally called `self.process.kill()` and would raise `AttributeError` in thread mode, failing loudly rather than continuing with two workers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: _create_process_for_shard is dead code with no callers and a misleading comment claiming it 'restarts that process' — calling it would re-create the process without killing the old one, and future wiring through it would inherit the duplicate-producer bug

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int)` (in `flusher.py`), but there are no callers shown anywhere in the diff, so it is dead code as introduced. Its comment says it will “restart that process”, but the implementation merely calls `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` without killing/terminating the existing `processes[process_index]`. Since `_create_process_for_shards` starts a new process/thread and then overwrites `self.processes[process_index]` with the new handle, calling `_create_process_for_shard` would leave the old worker running, which is misleading/dangerous behavior even if not currently exercised.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent metric tags: spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes use tag 'shard' while spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce uses 'shards' for the identical value, so dashboards/alerts keyed on one tag silently drop the other timer

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows inconsistent tag keys for the same shard identifier: `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timing("spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes", ..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})` but `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})`. This is verifiable in `SpanFlusher.main` and would cause metric series to be split across different tag dimensions, breaking dashboards/alerts expecting a consistent tag key.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Per-shard metric tag multiplies metric cardinality by shard count on every flush cycle — a hot-path tag explosion that should be capped or dropped

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds per-shard(-group) tags to hot-loop metrics in `SpanFlusher.main`, e.g. `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timing("spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes", ..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})`, where `shard_tag` is a comma-joined list of shard IDs (`",".join(map(str, shards))`). This increases metric series cardinality based on shard assignment (and potentially shard-group combinations across rebalances/process mappings). It’s not a functional correctness bug, but it is a concrete diff-introduced operational/observability concern (cardinality/perf/cost) that a reviewer could reasonably flag for capping/dropping/normalizing tags.

adjudication_records.issue_text: --flusher-processes 0 silently means 'unlimited': passing 0 falls through the 'or' to one-process-per-shard, the opposite of a cap, spawning up to len(assigned_shards) processes with no log or error

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats `0` as falsy. Since the new CLI option `--flusher-processes` is `type=int` with no validation, a user can pass `0`, which will then fall through to `len(buffer.assigned_shards)` and result in `num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(...)) == len(...)` (i.e., one process per shard), silently behaving like “unlimited” rather than a cap or an error.
